title: India Hilly Terrain Feasibility Study
scientific_rule: No Indian hilly disaster claim is justified without real Indian terrain data and externally validated metrics.
current_model_answer: No. The current model is not proven to work for Indian hilly regions.
why_current_model_fails: The model is building-centric and urban-scene-oriented rather than terrain-native.
The current Depth Anything V2 integration produces a relative depth prior, not a metric terrain sensor.
The calibration pipeline uses morphological and smoothing approximations that are not validated for steep terrain or landslide/flood scenarios.
The data pipeline has no Indian hilly benchmark or disaster-ground-truth suite.
The architecture does not model terrain, bare-earth, slope, vegetation, or hazard-specific outputs as first-class tasks.
components_reusable: Depth Anything V2 as a visual / relative-depth prior
Slope computation module for terrain inspection
Data ingestion and raster metadata handling
minimum_change_required: Add a terrain-aware branch and benchmark it on real Indian hilly data before any operational claim. A new terrain head or separate DTM/DEM pathway is required; the current building model must not be forced to act as a terrain model.
canny_help: Canny can help in a post-processing role for boundary refinement, but it is not a semantic terrain or building detector and is not a substitute for the actual model.
point_cloud_help: Point clouds can improve geometric continuity and terrain visualization, but only after the terrain height estimate is valid. They are an enhancement, not the root fix.
required_indian_data: landslide inventory or flood extent labels
held-out test region with no leakage
next_experiment: Run a minimal Indian hilly benchmark with a held-out test region, stratified by slope and terrain type, and separately report building, terrain, and hazard-related metrics.
do_not_change: Do not retrain or modify the production model in this phase.
Do not claim Indian generalization without real reference data.
Do not force the building-conditioned U-Net to masquerade as a terrain model.
Do not optimize the demo instead of the scientific benchmark.
fastest_defensible_path: Audit current architecture, acquire one small public Indian hilly benchmark with DEM truth, measure terrain-specific error, and then decide whether a terrain-aware branch or a simpler DEM-anchored extension is required.

use_cases.A_landslide_terrain_visualization: Requires new model capability and terrain validation
use_cases.B_flood_terrain_elevation_visualization: Requires external data and terrain calibration
use_cases.C_slope_and_steepness_analysis: Partially supported with current slope module; requires validation
use_cases.D_terrain_change_visualization: Requires external data and event-aware reference
use_cases.E_building_exposure_in_hazardous_terrain: Potentially feasible with terrain + building fusion, but not current out-of-box
use_cases.F_rapid_3d_reconstruction_after_disaster: Possible in a limited sense, but requires validated terrain + event data
use_cases.G_elevation_aware_disaster_simulation: Requires a full terrain-aware model and external physical priors

questions_answered.1: Can our CURRENT model work for Indian hilly regions? No.
questions_answered.2: If not, exactly why? Because it is building-centric, not terrain-native, and lacks real Indian terrain validation.
questions_answered.3: Which components can be reused? RGB, georeferencing, relative depth prior, DTM/DSM concepts, slope module, 3D visualization.
questions_answered.4: What is the minimum change required? A terrain-aware branch plus real benchmark validation.
questions_answered.5: Can Canny help? Only as a low-level post-processing aid.
questions_answered.6: Can point clouds help? Yes, for geometry continuity, but only after terrain truth is valid.
questions_answered.7: What Indian data do we need? DEM/DSM, optical imagery, slope and hazard labels, held-out benchmark splits.
questions_answered.8: What experiment should we run next? Minimal Indian hilly benchmark with terrain-specific metrics and slope stratification.
questions_answered.9: What should we NOT change? Do not retrain or claim Indian readiness before benchmark validation.
questions_answered.10: What is the fastest scientifically defensible path? Benchmark first, then add terrain-aware branch only if required by evidence.
